data.title: Design Distributed AI Model Downloader
data.contentPreview:
## 1. 🌐 What is a distributed model downloader?

A *distributed model downloader* is an internal data center tool that fetches a large ML model from an external repository and replicates it across every GPU host in a cluster. Because models can exceed hundreds of gigabytes and clusters contain hundreds to thousands of hosts, a naive serial approach would take hours. The challenge is to exploit parallelism within bandwidth constraints so that every host receives a complete, verified copy in minutes rather than hours.

## 2. Requirements

We are designing a system that downloads a 500 GB ML model from an external repository and replicates it across every host in a 1000-host cluster as fast as possible. The core product tension is minimizing the total distribution time to avoid idle GPU resources while operating under strict network bandwidth caps.

### Clarifying Questions

::::qa-item
:::you[You]
"When the platform is requested to distribute a model, should the system orchestrate and execute the full download to the hosts on-demand, or is it expected to run a continuous, background synchronization of all registry models?"
:::
:::interviewer[Interviewer]
"On-demand. We only distribute specific model versions when requested by our orchestration plane. Running a continuous background sync of the entire model registry is out of scope."
:::
:::takeaway[Takeaway]
An on-demand command-driven model keeps the downloader decoupled from the model registry's catalog, letting us focus on the distribution mechanics for a specific target model.
:::
::::

::::qa-item
:::you[You]
"Is the goal to minimize total distribution time as aggressively as possible, approaching a theoretical bandwidth limit, or is it sufficient to finish within a fixed SLA window like 10 to 20 minutes?"
:::
:::interviewer[Interviewer]
"Minimize total time. Every extra minute the cluster spends waiting for a model delays serving traffic with the updated version. We want to approach the bandwidth limit of our infrastructure, not just beat a loose target."
:::
:::takeaway[Takeaway]
The goal of minimizing wall-clock time forces us to design a highly parallel transfer topology that saturates available network links, rather than simply meeting a loose timeout.
:::
::::

::::qa-item
:::you[You]
"Is the external bandwidth limit a hard shared cap for all hosts combined, or does each host have its own independent link to the external model repository?"
:::
:::interviewer[Interviewer]
"Hard shared cap. The external link into the data center is 10 GB/s total. If multiple hosts download from the external repo at the same time, they divide that 10 GB/s between them."
:::
:::takeaway[Takeaway]
A shared external bottleneck implies that concurrent external pulls do not increase total throughput. We must designate a small set of seed hosts to fetch the data first, and then distribute it internally.
:::
::::
